Ibrany New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ibrány, Hungary

Not demolished. The newer of Ibrány's two Jewish cemeteries, undocumented on 19th-century cadastral maps, holds tombstones from 1917 through at least 1944. Ibrány's Jewish population grew from 201 (of 2,847 residents) in 1880 to 232 by 1941; a Jewish school was founded by Mór Bleuer, and in 1893 the community built a synagogue with construction help from local Christian farmers who transported materials from Kemecse - the building has since been demolished. By 1944, 214 Jews remained (33 taxpayers) before confinement to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto and deportation to Auschwitz.
